text:
sahil: heads up — we're seeing a spike of TLS connection resets from APAC (iOS) to api.redwood.example.com since ~2026-03-17 03:00 UTC. CS shows clients on IPv6-only carrier. 5xx rate from region jumped ~10x.

infra-bot: alert: TargetGroup unhealthy api-edge-apac-tg (3/5 failed HC) — last fail reason: connection reset

maria: do we have AAAA for api.redwood.example.com? carriers will synthesize via DNS64 if not.

sahil: quick dig from my laptop:
```
$ dig +short AAAA api.redwood.example.com @8.8.8.8

# nothing returned (expected)

$ dig +short AAAA api.redwood.example.com @our-dns
64:ff9b::c000:2001
```
looks like DNS64 synthesized AAAA. backend is A-only.

alex: checked infra — our ALB frontend is dualstack but target group type for api-edge-apac-tg is "instance" (IPv4-only). That means the LB accepts v6 conn but translates to IPv4; health checks are failing and connections are getting reset. Also saw envoy proxy change in last deploy that tightened SNI handling (reject if SNI missing).

katie: yep, during yesterday's deploy we added a hard-fail for TLS handshakes without SNI to mitigate SNI-stripping. Some carrier NAT64 translators (or client stacks) appear to open TLS without SNI, which hits the proxy and gets rejected.

ops-oncall: reproducer from a nat64 path:
```
$ curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:64:ff9b::c000:2001 https://api.redwood.example.com/
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.example.com/
*   Trying 64:ff9b::c000:2001...
* TCP connection established
* TLS handshake starts
* TLS alert: no_ssl_for_host
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
```

sahil: that matches the app logs: `tls: client did not send SNI` -> proxy returns 400, backend then appears unhealthy to the ALB -> 5xx cascade.

nat64-prober: ran active probes from our nat64 pool -> backend connection aborted, target flagged unhealthy after 4/5 fails.

maria: mitigation options: 1) revert the strict SNI check (fast), 2) switch to IP target groups + NLB (TCP passthrough) so we don't terminate/rewrite TLS at ALB, 3) publish AAAA records for the edge (but our origin can't serve v6 directly without infra changes).

alex: ops notes: creating IP target groups and an NLB dualstack per region avoids MALFORMED translation because the NLB will preserve the client connection (no TLS termination), but it means proxy sees original SNI and IP family. Work item to convert tg + move healthchecks.

katie: short term I prefer a rollback of the SNI strictness in envoy for APAC so we stop rejecting carrier-translated connections. We'll follow up with a safer check that tolerates absent SNI for known NAT64 prefixes.

ops-oncall: cost/ops question — enabling NLB dualstack + IP TG in APAC will add ~$1.2k/mo regionally (est). Need finance approval for full rollout; can canary in one region first.

maria: DNS trick of forcing IPv4 for mobile carriers is risky (EDNS steering/geo-split) — could fix some clients but will be a brittle band-aid.

ops-oncall: action items: 
1) rollback envoy SNI strictness for apac (sahil)
2) create canary IP target group + NLB in apac and route small % (alex)
3) run nat64 prober against canary and measure HC + 5xx reduction (nat64-prober / maria)
4) open cost approval ticket with finance for region add (ops-oncall)

sahil: +1, starting rollback now. @deploy-bot please roll back prod-edge-apac proxy config to prev commit.

deploy-bot: rollback triggered by sahil — started (deploy id: rb-2026-0317-01). ETA ~7m.

deploy-bot: rollback complete. Health checks recovered for api-edge-apac-tg, 5xx rate back to baseline. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks — canary NLB/TG workitem created (ENGINFRA-5921). Will tag for cost review.

maria: we'll keep the nat64 prober running and follow up tomorrow with a short post-mortem and recommended rollout plan.

ops-oncall: closing this thread; reopening if rollback fails or we see another spike. Thanks everyone. :heart:
